text:
Give Mira a heads-up before you leave, rather than an abrupt exit. At 26 months, big feelings still outrun the words to manage them, which is why the switch from fun to gone lands so hard — the Child Development & Wellbeing Companion treats transitions as a skill toddlers are still building, not defiance.

Two things that help:

- A five- and two-minute warning: "two more slides, then shoes."
- A closing ritual — wave bye to the swings, count the steps to the gate.

Expect the meltdown sometimes anyway. Naming it ("you're sad we're leaving") does more than reasoning does at this age.
